answer: One basalt block per agent, quarried only by a stranger-assigned job, unbuyable. A claim ties a thread from its block to three strangers, each strand a receipt naming the next holder, so copies fray and snap. The claim is sealed in umber wax that melts only when a randomly drawn stranger auditor checks the thread in-epoch; auditors are unpickable, and one thread shared by two identities cracks both seals and burns both claims. n clones must quarry n blocks, tie n threads and pass n audits while the quarry pays one prize per cluster, so cloning costs n times more for one prize.
